english.title: Conspire to carry / remove / deposit / harbour / keep / conceal / deal with chargeable goods intending to defraud HM
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) conspired together with

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSONS..)]_
(C)_[another person]_
(D)_[other persons]_

to be knowingly concerned in

(E)_[carrying]_
(F)_[removing]_
(G)_[depositing]_
(H)_[harbouring]_
(I)_[keeping]_
(J)_[concealing]_
(K)_[dealing with]_

goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..), which were chargeable with duty which had not been paid with intent defraud His Majesty of duty payable on the goods
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(b) and (3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) Any goods in respect of which an offence under this section is committed shall be liable to forfeiture, see section 170(6) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
